minutes.headline: Parks Commission backed a grants spreadsheet, a Marshall Park survey and a special town meeting engineering request.
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission heard a long facilities director update, then discussed grant options, space for Parks and Recreation in the building reuse plans, and the special town meeting warrant article for Marshall Park engineering. It reviewed a draft Marshall Park survey and set a posted meeting for November 1 and a regular meeting for November 16. The only formal votes captured were approving the September minutes and adjourning.

budget_items.what_was_said: Original capital plan placed a larger sum for both projects; beach treatment now estimated lower and put in this year's plan, with pond work planned later.

budget_items.what_was_said: Chair suggested a per-participant fee to help cover extra costs of indoor use.
Chair listed USDA, state parks, land and water, trail, dog park, ADA and AARP grants, with possible matching using ARPA funds.

budget_items.topic: Special town meeting article for engineering
budget_items.what_was_said: Select board request for engineering funding discussed, with a small remainder from a prior request; needs two-thirds vote.
Chair said the town manager indicated the bulk of the money is tax revenue, and recalled the spring appropriation was less than requested.

decisions.decision: Indoor soccer clinic to be pursued as a Parks program with public registration, about six weeks from January, up to 20 kids.
Chair will build a grants spreadsheet with deadlines and steps for the commission to review.
Commission will remind the building reuse committee that Parks and Recreation exists and needs flexible space, not dedicated space; a member to speak at a meeting.
A member will draft materials for the special town meeting presentation, with the chair reviewing.
Marshall Park survey to be distributed via town page, parks page and the recreation registration system.
Post a meeting for November 1 to join the select board in acknowledging a departing volunteer's service; next regular meeting November 16.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission discussed the select board's special town meeting article for Marshall Park engineering funding, and a member was assigned to draft presentation materials.
The commission agreed the Marshall Park survey will go out through the town page, the parks page and the recreation registration system.
The chair will build a grants spreadsheet of deadlines and steps, covering several federal and state options and possible matching with ARPA funds.
The commission will remind the building reuse committee that Parks and Recreation needs flexible space, not dedicated space.
The only formal votes recorded were approving the September minutes and adjourning; the other items were consensus or assignments.

why_it_matters: The engineering request for Marshall Park is headed to a special town meeting, where it needs a two-thirds vote, so residents may be asked to vote on it.
Parks and Recreation space in the building reuse plans and the grants list could shape what facilities and programs the town offers and how much of the cost lands on the tax-funded town budget.
